title: Private Deploy Field Compatibility Matrix and CAT (Customer Acceptance Tests) - 2026
author: Marcus Lee
content:
Overview:

This document provides a pragmatic compatibility matrix and a runnable Customer Acceptance Test (CAT) checklist for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem) of Redwood Inference. It aggregates constraints and tested compatibility across: OS/kernel, GPU models and drivers, container runtimes, networking (VPC/NAT/MTU), storage tiers and mount options, KMS/HSM integration, observability agents, and upgrade/rollback constraints. The goal is to give engineering and sales teams a single reference to determine whether a prospective customer environment is supported, requires mitigations, or is unsupported.

When to use this page:
- Pre-sales validation for dedicated/private offers
- Onboarding architecture review with customer infra teams
- Day‑2 operations planning for upgrades/migrations

Compatibility summary (status legend):
- SUPPORTED: Redwood has validated and recommends this configuration for production.
- SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS: Works but with tradeoffs (reduced throughput, feature flags disabled, additional runbook steps).
- UNSUPPORTED: Not recommended; significant engineering effort required.

High-level compatibility matrix (text table):

| Component category | Key items tested | Recommended versions / settings | Status | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Host OS | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, RHEL 8.9, Rocky 8.6 | Ubuntu 22.04 preferred; kernel >= 5.15 | SUPPORTED | We test packages on these images. Custom kernels require validation. |
| GPUs | NVIDIA A10, A100 40GB, H100, RTX 6000 | Driver 525+ (A100 use 520/525+, H100 535+), CUDA 11.8+ | SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS | H100: require runtime build with newer attention kernels; contact Redwood for optimized image. |
| Container runtime | containerd 1.6+, Docker 20.10+ (runtime: runc/CRI) | Use containerd for cluster installation; Docker supported for single-host. | SUPPORTED | We ship OCI images.
| Orchestration | Kubernetes 1.25–1.29 | kubelet flags: --feature-gates=..., runtimeClass enabled | SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS | Older K8s may need custom admission.
| Networking (VPC) | Private subnet w/ NAT, egress via managed NAT gateway | MTU >= 1500, bandwidth >= 10 Gbps for medium clusters | SUPPORTED | For burst workloads use dedicated egress links. |
| MTU and tunneling | VXLAN/GRE overlay | MTU 1400+ recommended; fragmentation causes latency | SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS | If MTU < 1400 expect ~10–30% throughput drop. |
| Storage | Local NVMe (>= 1 TB for model cache), NFS backed by EBS/CSI | XFS recommended for NVMe; ext4 ok for experimental | SUPPORTED | NFS: ensure fsync latency < 10ms for prompt-serving. |
| KMS / HSM | AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, BYO-HSM (PKCS#11) | TLS mutual auth, key rotation window: 90d | SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS | BYO-HSM requires a tested connector (scheduling & failover runbook). |
| TLS | TLS 1.2, TLS 1.3 | Prefer TLS1.3, ciphers: ECDHE+AESGCM | SUPPORTED | Mutual TLS required for some private control-planes. |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry Collector, Prometheus, Grafana | otel-collector v0.60+, prometheus 2.40+ | SUPPORTED | Sampling and PII redaction required for regulated customers. |
| RBAC / IAM | OIDC & SAML SSO | OIDC preferred for short-lived tokens | SUPPORTED | SAML still supported via SSO proxy. |
| Quantized runtimes | int8/4-bit quantization pipelines | Requires runtime flags and validated model artifacts | SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS | Certain attention kernels revert to slower paths; test with cust prompts. |

Operational thresholds and Day‑2 constraints:

- Minimum telemetry retention for root-cause: 7 days full-span traces, 30 days aggregated metrics.
- Alerting thresholds (recommendation):
  - P95 serving latency > 250ms for 60s => page SRE team
  - Token error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m => trigger rollback plan
  - OOM events > 1/hour per node => scale policy or instance type change

Customer Acceptance Test (CAT) checklist (runnable steps):

1) Environment validation (infra):
   - Confirm OS kernel:
     uname -a
   - Confirm GPU presence and drivers:
     nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version --format=csv
   - Check available NVMe capacity and latency:
     lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,MOUNTPOINT
     sudo fio --name=nvme-latency --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --rw=randread --bs=4k --size=1G --numjobs=4 --time_based --runtime=30

2) Container and networking validation:
   - Validate MTU and path MTU discovery:
     ip link show && ip route get 8.8.8.8
   - Simple network throughput test (iperf3):
     iperf3 -c <server> -P 8 -t 30

3) Model-serving smoke test (single-host):
   - Pull Redwood runtime image and run quick generator test:
     docker run --rm -e RW_API_KEY=test -p 8000:8000 ghcr.io/redwood-inference/runtime:stable-2026-01 
     curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-open-compat","prompt":"Say hi"}' | jq

4) Observability and audit trace validation:
   - Confirm metrics exported to Prometheus:
     curl -sS http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep redwood_runtime
   - Verify trace export to OTLP collector using sample trace generator (curl to /v1/trace/test)

5) KMS integration test:
   - Rotate test key with 1-hour TTL and attempt signing operations via runtime CLI. Confirm logs show key usage and no timeouts.

Upgrade and rollback constraints (practical runbook summary):

- Pre-upgrade gating checks (all must pass):
  1. No active canary > 5% of production traffic for 10m.
  2. All nodes have < 10% CPU pressure and < 70% GPU memory used.
  3. Telemetry ingestion backfill window healthy (no API backlog).

- Online upgrade pattern (recommended for K8s):
  1. Canary deploy new runtime to 1 node / 5% capacity. Run CAT subset of tests for 15 minutes.
  2. If canary OK, gradually increase 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 10m observation windows.
  3. If token-error-rate increases or latency regressions exceed thresholds, trigger immediate rollback.

- Rollback checklist (if upgrade fails):
  1. Shift traffic to previous model variant via routing policy.
  2. Re-provision previous runtime image on failed nodes and validate model cache warmup.
  3. Run smoke test suite; collect and attach logs and traces to incident ticket.

Known incompatibilities and mitigation strategies:

- Low MTU networks (MTU <= 1400):
  - Effect: Increased fragmentation, higher per-token latency and throughput loss.
  - Mitigation: Enable jumbo frames on overlay or pin runtime to host networking where possible.

- Custom or older CUDA stacks (CUDA < 11.5):
  - Effect: Unsupported kernel paths; quantized runtime will fallback to slower code paths.
  - Mitigation: Upgrade drivers and CUDA where possible; otherwise schedule a performance tuning engagement.

- HSM behind network proxies with aggressive timeouts:
  - Effect: Key operations timeout during bursty workloads.
  - Mitigation: Tune proxy idle/timeouts and add local caching layer for key material with strict TTL.

Acceptance metrics and sign-off:

- Minimum performance sign‑off (example for medium deployment):
  - 95th percentile latency for 1k token prompt: < 600ms
  - Throughput: sustain 200 concurrent small requests (2–8 tokens output) with <10% degradation from baseline
  - Error budget: token error rate < 0.5% in steady-state test window

- Customer sign-off steps:
  1. Run CAT (items 1–5) with Redwood Solutions Engineer present.
  2. Validate upgrade/rollback dry run with simulated traffic.
  3. Approve cutover schedule, maintenance window, and post-cutover monitoring runbook.

Ownership and escalation paths:

- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments - Solutions Engineering (onboarding lead)
- Escalation: If CAT fails, open ticket in our customer-onboarding queue and page oncall SRE (use /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets for SLOs).

Appendix A: Example Helm values for small on‑prem cluster (text snippet):

replicaCount: 2
image:
  repository: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/runtime
  tag: stable-2026-01
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  requests:
    cpu: "4000m"
    memory: "16Gi"
nodeSelector:
  rtx: "true"
securityContext:
  runAsUser: 1000

Appendix B: Troubleshooting quick commands:

- Check runtime logs:
  kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/redwood-runtime -c runtime --since=15m
- Check model cache hit rate (promql):
  rate(redwood_model_cache_hits_total[5m]) / rate(redwood_model_cache_requests_total[5m])

Appendix C: Contact matrix and SLAs for private deployments:

- Solutions Engineering (onboarding): se-onboarding@redwood.ai (primary)
- SRE Pager: +1-555-0132 (use for Sev1/2 during cutovers)

Document maintenance notes:

- This compatibility matrix is updated quarterly or on every major runtime release.
- Add new GPU families, runtime flags, or customer workarounds as validated by Redwood test lab.
